description: A low‐relief, almost rectangular embanked platform with straight margins visible in the hillshade, roughly 350 m east–west by 200 m north–south. The edges are aligned to the local grid (approximately N85°E) and are defined by subtle scarps 0.3–0.5 m high. In the NIR overlay the interior shows a slightly higher moisture signature compared to the surrounding forest, consistent with anthropogenic dark‐earth retention.

A sinuous, low‐relief linear depression running roughly north–south through the center of the scene. It extends for ~500 m, is ~5–8 m wide, and appears as a dark line in the NIR band (higher moisture) and as a faint concave trench in the DTM-derived hillshade. Its course bypasses natural gullies, suggesting an engineered canal.

A smaller rectilinear enclosure (~150 m × 120 m) in the southeastern quadrant. Visible as paired linear ridges in the slope curvature derivative, with a corresponding moisture anomaly in the NIR image. Likely a subsidiary raised plot or diversion channel.
